scenario_summary: Version conflict: two DPA versions are both included in the package (v1, effective 2024-01-10, 30-day retention; v2, effective 2025-06-01, 60-day retention) with no changelog or note explaining or superseding the earlier figure. Tests whether document versioning is tracked and whether the system recognizes this as a package-level inconsistency rather than silently preferring whichever document it reads last.

claims.subject: data retention after termination (v1)
claims.source_excerpt: Upon termination, Brindle shall delete all customer personal data within 30 days.
claims.evidence_requirement: Consistency with any other version of this same document in the package.

evidence_items.excerpt: Upon termination, Brindle shall delete all customer personal data within 60 days.

claims.expected_handling_notes: Both DPA versions are present in the same package with different retention figures and no reconciling changelog. A correct system should not silently treat the later-dated document (v2) as automatically authoritative and discard v1's figure without comment — the absence of a changelog explaining the change is itself part of what should be flagged to the human reviewer, since it's unclear whether v2 is a deliberate policy change or an error.

claims.subject: data retention after termination (v2)
claims.source_excerpt: Upon termination, Brindle shall delete all customer personal data within 60 days.
claims.evidence_requirement: Consistency with any other version of this same document in the package.

evidence_items.excerpt: Upon termination, Brindle shall delete all customer personal data within 30 days.

claims.expected_handling_notes: Same conflict as c1, viewed from the newer version. Both should be linked by the same expected_conflicts entry.

expected_conflicts.description: Two DPA versions in the same package state different retention periods (30 vs. 60 days) with no changelog or note reconciling the change.
